Mali.title: Mali: Russia deploys Lancet kamikaze drones against rebels
Mali.summary: The Russian Africa Corps has carried out at least ten strikes with ZALA Lancet kamikaze drones in Mali since April, according to an analysis by the US research centre Conflict Insights Group (CIG) released on 19 November 2024. Each attack identified involved the Lancet alongside a surveillance drone from the same manufacturer. As such, CIG presents this equipment as a new addition this year.

Mali.title: Koulikoro: Curfew extended until 20 December
Mali.summary: The Governor of the Koulikoro region has renewed the curfew for one month, from 21 November to 20 December 2026. The curfew still applies to the entire region, from midnight to 5 a.m. During these hours, movement is prohibited.

Mali.title: ARMY GENERAL STAFF: The DOSAM project alongside the Defence and Security Forces
Mali.summary: The General Staff of the Army, in collaboration with the Association of Former Pupils of the Prytanée Militaire de Kati, through its DOSAM (Blood and Medicine Donation) project, organised a blood donation day on Friday, 20 November 2026, at its premises. The event was chaired by Colonel Doctor Marius SANOU, Chief Medical Officer of the Army Garrison Medical Centre, in the presence of several military authorities.

Mali.title: Mali: The inside story of the “release” of soldiers held captive by the separatist FLA group
Mali.summary: Mali: The story behind the "release" of soldiers held captive by the separatist FLA group In Mali, on 18 November, the army claimed the release of 24 soldiers held near In-Tebezas, in the Kidal region. . According to the General Staff's statement, it was an operation carried out jointly with its “partners” – the Russian Africa Corps is not named – which made it possible to “neutralise” the “elements” of the “terrorist groups” and to free these soldiers.

Mali.title: DIRECTORATE OF MILITARY COLLEGES: The 2026–2027 academic year at the Military Colleges has officially begun
Mali.summary: On Thursday, 19 November 2026, the parade ground of the Boubacar Sada SY Training Centre in Koulikoro hosted the formal ceremony marking the start of the 2026–2027 academic year for the Military Colleges. The ceremony was presided over by the Director of Military Colleges, Brigadier General Moussa Yoro Kanté, in the presence of several military and administrative officials, senior officers, and students and trainees from the various training establishments.

Mali.title: Mali: The Malian army announces the release of 24 soldiers during a special operation near Kidal
Mali.summary: The General Staff of the Malian Armed Forces announced the release, on Wednesday, 18 November, of twenty-four (24) soldiers from the Malian Armed Forces (FAMa) who had been held hostage in the Kidal region, following an air-land operation. The operation took place on Wednesday, 18 November, at around 1 p.m. in the In-Tebezas area, located approximately 110 kilometres southeast of Kidal.

Mali.source: AMAP (Agence Malienne de Presse et de Publicité)
Mali.title: KAYES: A NEW CONVOY OF TANKERS ARRIVES UNDER FAMa ESCORT
Mali.summary: Kayes, 19 November (AMAP) – A new convoy of fuel tankers arrived in the city of Kayes on Thursday, 19 November 2020, escorted by the Malian Armed Forces (FAMa), announced the Regional Directorate of the General Directorate for Trade, Consumer Affairs and Competition (DGCC). According to the same source, these petroleum products are intended to supplement the stocks already available at service stations and points of sale in the region.

Mali.title: Analysis: Russia's "Africa Corps" uses a new drone as operations escalate in Mali
Mali.summary: A new analysis, seen by Reuters, has revealed that the Russian Africa Corps forces operating in Mali deployed a new type of armed drone this year, at a time when they intensified their airstrikes in an attempt to regain the momentum they lost following an attack by extremist and separatist militants in April.

Mali.title: The International Crisis Group recommends negotiations between the Sahelian military regimes and JNIM
Mali.summary: . "The Battle for the Cities: Countering the JNIM Threat to Sahel Urban Centres" is the title of the report published this Friday, 20 November, by the International Crisis Group (ICG), a non-governmental research organisation specialising in conflict prevention and analysis. .

Mali.title: Gao: One dead and three injured in an explosive device blast in Edang
Mali.summary: One child lost his life and three people were seriously injured, including two children, in the explosion of an explosive device this Thursday at around 3 p.m. in the village of Edang, Anchawadj commune, Gao region. According to local sources, children are said to have picked up the device before handing it over to a scrap metal dealer.

Mali.source: AMAP (Agence Malienne de Presse et de Publicité)
Mali.title: Kayes: A new convoy of tanker trucks boosts hydrocarbon stocks
Mali.summary: Kayes, 19 November (AMAP) The City of Railways has just witnessed the arrival, this Thursday, of a new convoy of tanker trucks, escorted by our valiant Malian Armed Forces (FAMa), who were once again commended by the Regional Directorate of Trade for their commitment and courage, as reported by AMAP. “These products supplement the stocks already available at service stations and points of sale, and confirm the continuity and regularity of fuel supplies throughout the Kayes Region”, said the Regional Director of Trade.

Mali.title: Russia's Africa Corps deploys new drone in Mali as strikes increase, analysis says
Mali.summary: Reuters

Burkina Faso.title: Côte d'Ivoire-Burkina Faso: Camille Makosso, the "general" who is challenging Ibrahim Traoré
Burkina Faso.summary: Côte d'Ivoire-Burkina Faso: Camille Makosso, the "general" who is defying Ibrahim Traoré Targeted by the Burkinabé justice system, the Ivorian pastor-influencer asserts his loyalty to President Alassane Ouattara. From Conakry to Cotonou, this former gang leader, who has been imprisoned twice, is building political influence through a combination of preaching and spectacle.

Burkina Faso.title: Image Published on 20 November 2026 Africa Sahel: The ICG think tank advocates dialogue between states and JNIM jihadists The International Crisis Group (ICG) think tank recommended on Friday that the Sahel states engage in dialogue with JNIM jihadists…
Burkina Faso.summary: Burkinabé soldiers in Ouagadougou, 8 October 2022. On Friday, the think tank International Crisis Group (ICG) recommended that the Sahel countries engage in dialogue with the jihadists of JNIM, stating in a report that a military victory appears "out of reach", after more than a decade of conflict. .

Burkina Faso.title: Burkina Faso: The celebration of 11 December 2026 announced to “reaffirm national sovereignty”
Burkina Faso.summary: The Burkinabé government has announced the celebration of 11 December 2026 to "reaffirm national sovereignty", among other things, according to the report of the Council of Ministers on Thursday, 19 November. . It was Burkina Faso's Minister of Justice, Mr Edasso Rodrigue Bayala, who was acting as Minister of State, Minister of Territorial Administration and Mobility, who addressed the Council on the celebration of 11 December 2026, under the theme 'Popular progressive revolution in Burkina Faso: a recognition of resistance to colonial domination and imperialism'.

Burkina Faso.title: Burkina Faso: A major military parade announced in Ouagadougou for 11 December 2026
Burkina Faso.summary: At its meeting on Thursday, 19 November 2026, the Council of Ministers considered a communication concerning the celebration of 11 December 2026. This year's event will be held under the theme 'The People's Progressive Revolution in Burkina Faso: a celebration of resistance to colonial domination and imperialism'. According to the minutes of the Council of Ministers, this celebration aims to reaffirm national sovereignty and to demonstrate, before the people of Burkina Faso and the international community, full control over the nation's destiny.

Burkina Faso.title: Burkina Faso: Minutes of the Council of Ministers meeting held on Thursday, 19 November 2026
Burkina Faso.summary: The Council of Ministers met in Ouagadougou on Thursday, 19 November 2026, in an ordinary session, from 9:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m., under the chairmanship of Comrade Captain Ibrahim TRAORE, President of Burkina Faso, President of the Council of Ministers. It deliberated on the items on its agenda, heard oral reports, made appointments, and authorised missions abroad.

Burkina Faso.title: Burkina Faso/Security: Minister Mahamadou Sana focuses on pooling resources and coordinating action to enhance effectiveness (…)
Burkina Faso.summary: Burkina Faso/Security: Minister Mahamadou Sana focuses on pooling resources and coordinating action to enhance the effectiveness of the forces. The Minister of Security, Mahamadou Sana, chaired the proceedings of the 2nd Ministerial Sector Board (CASEM) for Security on Friday, 20 November 2026, in Ouagadougou. This meeting is being held on the theme "Pooling of resources and synergy of action between the security forces: a strategic imperative for an integrated and effective response to security challenges".

Burkina Faso.title: Minutes of the Council of Ministers meeting held on Thursday, 19 November 2026
Burkina Faso.summary: The Council of Ministers met in Ouagadougou on Thursday, 19 November 2026, in an ordinary session, from 9:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m., under the chairmanship of Comrade Captain Ibrahim TRAORE, President of Faso, President of the Council of Ministers. It deliberated on the items on its agenda, heard oral reports, made appointments, and authorised missions abroad.

Burkina Faso.title: Burkina Faso: Report of the Council of Ministers meeting held on Thursday, 19 November 2026
Burkina Faso.summary: Burkina Faso: Report of the Council of Ministers of Thursday, 19 November 2026 The Council of Ministers met in Ouagadougou on Thursday, 19 November 2026, in an ordinary session, from 9:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m., under the chairmanship of Comrade Captain Ibrahim Traoré, President of Burkina Faso and Chairman of the Council of Ministers. .

Niger.title: Niger: What we know about the fuel convoy escorted by Algeria
Niger.summary: A few days after the vote on 25 October 2026 in the Algerian Parliament authorising the dispatch of military units to Niger to 'secure energy interests', a first fuel convoy, accompanied by a military escort, entered Niger, heading for Agadez, in the north of the country. During the few days of confirmed Algerian military presence on the ground, a lot of fake news spread on social media.

Niger.title: Dosso: The Minister of Agriculture and Livestock at the irrigated sites of Dallol
Niger.summary: Dosso, 20 November (ANP) – On Thursday, 19 November, the Minister of Agriculture and Livestock, Colonel Bilaly Gambo, accompanied by the Governor of the Dosso Region, the Director General of the National Office for Hydro-Agricultural Development (ONAHA), senior officials from the Ministry, Regional Directors, and officials from the Defence and Security Forces, carried out a field visit to several developed irrigated sites.

Mali.title: AES: Burkinabe officers on a study visit to Mali to strengthen military cooperation
Mali.summary: Trainees from the Staff College of Burkina Faso arrived at Modibo-Keïta International Airport in Sénou, Bamako, on Thursday, 19 November 2026. The group is led by Colonel-Major Céleste Joseph Moussa Coulibaly, Commandant of the Higher Military Education Institute. .

Mali.title: AES: Mali welcomes the second class of the Burkina Faso Staff College
Mali.summary: The second class of the Burkina Faso Staff College arrived at Modibo-KEÏTA International Airport in Sénou, Bamako, on Thursday, 19 November 2026. Led by the Commandant of the Institute of Higher Military Education of Burkina Faso, Colonel-Major Céleste Joseph Moussa COULIBALY, the delegation was welcomed by Colonel-Major Drissa Salifou DEMBÉLÉ, Deputy Chief of Staff in charge of General Studies and External relations.

Mali.title: Kidal: The army announces the release of 24 soldiers in In-Tebezas
Mali.summary: RIGHT NOW The announcement came on the evening of 18 November, a few hours after the operation carried out in an area southeast of Kidal. The soldiers in question were being held by an armed group whose identity has not been specified. The official account states that an aerial reconnaissance mission identified the place of detention and the armed positions.

Mali.title: Douentza: Rural women in the spotlight
Mali.summary: This Thursday, the Maison des Arts et de la Culture in Douentza hosted a meeting dedicated to recognising the contribution of women to rural activities. Coming from the various municipalities and localities of the region, they displayed cereals from their own production. .

Mali.title: Gao: One dead and three injured in an explosive device blast in Edang
Mali.summary: One child lost his life and three people were seriously injured, including two children, in the explosion of an explosive device on Thursday at around 3 p.m. in the village of Edang, Anchawadj commune, Gao region. According to local sources, children reportedly picked up the device before handing it over to a scrap metal dealer.

Mali.title: Mali: The FAMA free 24 soldiers held by terrorists in Kidal
Mali.summary: According to information reported by the Malian Press Agency (AMAP), the Malian Armed Forces (FAMA) carried out a military operation yesterday, Wednesday 18 November, in the In-Tebezas area, about 110 km southeast of Kidal. This offensive led to the release of 24 soldiers held hostage by armed terrorist groups. .

Mali.title: The Malian army announces the “killing” of armed men in airstrikes near Kidal and Nono
Mali.summary: The Malian army announced that it had carried out airstrikes targeting positions and gatherings of armed groups it described as terrorist in several areas, including the vicinity of Kidal and Nono. These strikes were part of Operation Dogokoloko and resulted in the deaths of several militants. In a statement issued on Thursday, 19 November, the army clarified that, with the support of its partners, the Malian Armed Forces had targeted a camp on Tuesday containing militants and logistical equipment, including motorcycles, located 15 kilometres southeast of Nono.

Mali.title: Niono, Sofara, Niafunké, Kidal: The army announces a series of strikes
Mali.summary: The Malian army is continuing its operations against armed terrorist groups. According to the General Staff of the Armed Forces, the Malian Armed Forces (FAMa) and their partners carried out several strikes on 17 and 18 November 2026, as part of Operation Dougoukoloko. 15 kilometres southeast of Niono, the army struck a terrorist camp .

Mali.title: Mali: 24 soldiers freed thanks to a special forces operation
Mali.summary: According to the General Staff of the Armed Forces, this meticulously prepared joint operation began with an aerial reconnaissance mission that identified the positions of the terrorist groups as well as the location where the hostages were being held. Following precise intelligence, airstrikes were carried out in the area of In-Tebezas, a locality located around a hundred kilometres from the town of Kidal.

Mali.source: AMAP (Agence Malienne de Presse et de Publicité)
Mali.title: Counter-Terrorism: Strikes by the National Defence Forces in Several Parts of the Country
Mali.summary: Bamako, 19 November (AMAP) The Malian Armed Forces (FAMa), supported by their partners, are continuing their operations to monitor, control and secure the national territory as part of Operation Dougoukoloko. Several positions and logistical resources of armed terrorist groups were targeted, with results deemed satisfactory, according to a statement from the General Staff of the Armed Forces published on Thursday.

Mali.title: Mali: 24 soldiers released after airstrikes southeast of Kidal
Mali.summary: The Malian army has announced the release of 24 of its soldiers who were being held in the In-Tebezas area, southeast of Kidal. The operation, carried out on Wednesday, 18 November 2026, involved air assets and ground troops. The Malian Armed Forces (FAMa) have announced a military operation that led to the release of 24 of their personnel who were being held in the In-Tebezas area, located about 110 kilometres southeast of Kidal.

Mali.title: Operation Dougoukoloko: Several terrorist positions and resources targeted in Niono, Sofara, Niafunké and Kidal
Mali.summary: The General Staff of the Armed Forces informs the national public that the Malian Armed Forces (FAMa), supported by their partners, are continuing their ongoing operations to monitor, control and secure the national territory as part of Operation Dougoukoloko. . On Tuesday, 17 November 2026, a camp belonging to armed terrorist groups, housing several individuals as well as logistical equipment, including motorcycles, was targeted by precision strikes fifteen (15) kilometres southeast of Niono.

Mali.title: Mali: 24 soldiers freed during an army operation near Kidal
Mali.summary: On Wednesday, 18 November 2026, the Malian army announced the release of 24 of its soldiers held in the In-Tebezas area, about 110 kilometres southeast of Kidal, following an operation combining airstrikes and ground troop intervention. According to a statement from the General Staff of the Armed Forces, the operation was launched at around 1 p.m., following an aerial reconnaissance phase that enabled the positions of the armed groups to be located, as well as the site where the soldiers were being held.

Burkina Faso.title: Djibril Bassolé, Mamadou Alpha Barry, Ahmed Newton Barry… In Burkina Faso, behind the accusations of ‘terrorism’, the hunt for critical voices
Burkina Faso.summary: Djibril Bassolé, Mamadou Alpha Barry, Ahmed Newton Barry… In Burkina Faso, behind the accusations of 'terrorism', the hunt for critical voices The Burkinabé judiciary has unveiled a series of proceedings targeting prominent figures based abroad. Accused of "complicity in terrorism", several of them denounce an offensive aimed at silencing opponents of Ibrahim Traoré's junta.

Burkina Faso.title: Burkina Faso: Burkina Faso Targets Critics in Exile
Burkina Faso.summary: Junta's Arrest Warrants, Extradition Requests Extend Crackdown Abroad Journalists, activists and political opponents who fled Burkina Faso to escape the junta's repression now risk arrest and prosecution abroad, as the country's judicial authorities pursue dozens of individuals over alleged terrorism-related offenses. Burkina Faso Prosecutor General Désiré Sawadogo announced on November 13 that a special court handling terrorism-related offenses had opened six cases against at least 45 people and entities.

Niger.title: Niger: What we know about the fuel convoy escorted by Algeria
Niger.summary: A few days after the vote on 25 October 2023 in the Algerian Parliament approving the dispatch of military units to Niger to “secure energy interests”, a first fuel convoy, accompanied by a military escort, entered Niger, heading towards Agadez, in the north of the country. . During the few days of confirmed Algerian military presence on the ground, a lot of fake news spread on social media.

Niger.title: Nigeria: Nigeria, Cameroon, Chad, Niger Reach Deal On Military Pursuit of Terrorists
Niger.summary: Nigeria and three neighbouring countries -- Cameroon, Chad and Niger -- have reportedly agreed to allow military forces to pursue terrorists, armed bandits and other criminal groups up to five kilometres across their shared borders. The arrangement is aimed at strengthening regional counterterrorism operations and preventing fleeing militants from escaping military pressure by crossing into neighbouring territories.

Niger.title: Insecurity in the Dosso region: in Dioundou, the authorities denounce the involvement of "local children" in the recent series of massacres of civilians
Niger.summary: Last weekend, the Governor of Dosso visited the people mourning a series of massacres of civilians perpetrated by members of the terrorist group 'Lakurawa' in several villages in the Dioundou Department, in the Dosso Region. .

Mali.title: 22:03 Mali announces the release of 24 soldiers from captivity
Mali.summary: Today, Wednesday, the Malian army announced the liberation of 24 soldiers who had been held captive by armed groups in the north of the country during a joint military operation with its partners, which also resulted in the killing of several militants. In a statement reported by the Russian news agency RIA Novosti, the Malian Armed Forces explained that the operation was carried out in the In-Tebzas area, located about 110 kilometres southeast of the city of Kidal, and resulted in the liberation of the detained soldiers.

Mali.source: AMAP (Agence Malienne de Presse et de Publicité)
Mali.title: Kidal: 24 FAMa soldiers freed during an operation in In-Tebezas
Mali.summary: Bamako, 18 November (AMAP) – Twenty-four (24) Malian soldiers detained in the In-Tebezas area, around 110 kilometres southeast of Kidal, were released on Wednesday, 18 November 2020, thanks to a military operation carried out by the Malian Armed Forces (FAMa), with the support of their partners, the General Staff of the Armed Forces announced in a statement.

Mali.source: AMAP (Agence Malienne de Presse et de Publicité)
Mali.title: Ségou: Adama Téréta presents the national flag to the Governor
Mali.summary: Ségou, 18 November 2026 (AMAP) – Following a march through several localities in the Sikasso and Ségou regions, including Sikasso, Koutiala, M'Pessoba, Bla and Cinzana Gare, the marcher Adama Téréta symbolically handed over the national flag to the Governor of Ségou, Chiaka Magassa, on Wednesday. This march is part of an effort to promote peace, social cohesion and national reconciliation, explained Adama Téréta.

Mali.title: Kidal: 24 Malian soldiers released during a joint operation by the FAMa
Mali.summary: The General Staff of the Armed Forces informs the national public that, on Wednesday, 18 November 2020, at around 1 p.m., the Malian Armed Forces (FAMa) and their partners successfully carried out an operation to free twenty-four (24) FAMa soldiers being held in the In-Tebezas area, approximately one hundred and ten (110) kilometres southeast of Kidal. . Meticulously prepared, this joint operation began with an aerial reconnaissance that identified the positions of the armed terrorist groups, as well as the location where the hostages were being held.

Mali.title: Kidal: The army frees 24 soldiers held by armed groups
Mali.summary: Twenty-four Malian soldiers have regained their freedom. According to the General Staff of the Armed Forces, the Malian Armed Forces (FAMa) and their partners freed them on Wednesday, 18 November 2026, at around 1 p.m. The soldiers were being held in the In-Tebezas area, about 110 kilometres southeast of Kidal.

Mali.source: AMAP (Agence Malienne de Presse et de Publicité)
Mali.title: Macina: Holding a consultation forum to address concerns in the cercle
Mali.summary: Macina, 18 November (AMAP) The Cercle Prefect, Albaraka Ag Amarizag, met in the prefecture's conference room with the authorities and traditional leaders, the defence and security forces, the heads of technical departments, the umbrella organisations of civil society – in short, all those who have a say in the life of the town, as AMAP observed. There was only one item on the agenda, namely discussions between him and the traditional authorities, the heads of technical departments and the umbrella organisations of civil society.

Mali.title: Mali’s Air Force receives major boost with delivery of Il-76 transport aircraft, Mi-8 and Mi-24 helicopters
Mali.summary: Mali’s armed forces have received seven Russian-made aircraft, including an Ilyushin Il-76TD transport aircraft, four Mi-8 helicopters and two Mi-24 attack helicopters, as Bamako continues to expand its air mobility and combat-support capabilities. The aircraft were formally handed over at Modibo Keïta-Senou International Airport in Bamako on 16 November during a ceremony presided over by transitional President General Assimi Goïta, Mali’s commander-in-chief.

Mali.title: Nioro du Sahel: The efforts of the FAMa...
Mali.summary: Nioro du Sahel: The efforts of the FAMa are promoting the resumption of economic activities and transport The efforts of the Malian Armed Forces (FAMa) to improve security and facilitate the free movement of people and goods are contributing to the gradual return to normality in Nioro du Sahel. . The arrival of several dozen fuel tankers, the resumption of transport links with Bamako and Kayes, and the restocking of markets are all signs of this change after nine months of severe disruption.

Mali.title: Nioro du Sahel: FAMa's efforts are helping to revive economic activity and transport
Mali.summary: Transport companies have welcomed the resumption of the service. The arrival of several dozen fuel tankers, the resumption of transport links with Bamako and Kayes, and the restocking of markets are all signs of this development after nine months of severe disruption. .

Mali.title: Expelled from Guinea: More than 1,100 people still present at the Bamako site
Mali.summary: As part of the return operations, a lorry was mobilised on 16 November from the Kouremalé assembly site to transport around 110 people, including four to the Bamako District and 106 to Burkina Faso. On 17 November, the Burkinabé authorities also deployed 20 buses, two military trucks and 16 medical ambulances to ensure the care and return of their compatriots.

Mali.title: Road safety issues in Mali: 2 deaths and 33 serious injuries on the roads every day
Mali.summary: "2 deaths and 33 serious injuries every day on the roads". This alarming toll was highlighted by Ousmane Bah Maïga, Director General of the National Road Safety Agency (ANASER), on Sunday, 15 November 2026, in Bamako. This was during a training session held at the Maison de la Presse for 60 journalists from traditional media and digital platforms.

Mali.title: Mali: The FAMa target bases and logistics depots of armed groups in Abeïbara and Sévaré
Mali.summary: Maliweb

Mali.title: Bamako, the new battleground for influence, or why the AFRICOM Commander visited the arms fair...
Mali.summary: Bamako, the new battleground for influence, or why the AFRICOM Commander visited the arms fair in Mali Russia, Türkiye and the United States are continuing their rivalry for military and political influence in the Sahel. This is what the BAMEX defence and security exhibition, which has just taken place in Mali, demonstrates. .

Mali.title: Washington is preparing for the "biggest financial attack" on Iran, and the latter is threatening to respond "harshly".
Mali.summary: Washington prepares for "biggest financial attack" on Iran, which threatens to respond "harshly" DW.com

Burkina Faso.title: Burkina Faso Targets Critics in Exile
Burkina Faso.summary: Journalists, activists and political opponents who fled Burkina Faso to escape the junta’s repression now risk arrest and prosecution abroad, as the country’s judicial authorities pursue dozens of individuals over alleged terrorism-related offenses. Burkina Faso Prosecutor General Désiré Sawadogo announced on November 13 that a special court handling terrorism-related offenses had opened six cases against at least 45 people and entities.

Burkina Faso.title: Press Release | SN CITEC: Notice of recruitment of associations and organisations of stevedores in Bobo-Dioulasso
Burkina Faso.summary: Notice of Expression of Interest: No. 2026-33364/DG/NPK Recruitment of associations or organisations of stevedores on behalf of SN CITEC 1- Purpose of the services SN CITEC wishes to pre-select associations or organisations to carry out, at its sites, the loading, unloading and handling of raw materials, finished products and other goods, as well as their movement, storage and stacking .

Burkina Faso.title: Flow of underage children to gold mining sites: In Dédougou, “Polisi I Nisonisa” raises awareness
Burkina Faso.summary: Launched in March 2026 in the Bankui region, Polisi I Nisonisa, which means "the police, my neighbour" in Bwamu, is a community policing initiative that focuses on dialogue and proximity to enhance security. As part of this approach, its teams visit neighbourhoods and public places to engage with local residents about their security concerns. .

Niger.title: Tahoua: Significant quantity of weapons and ammunition seized in Ibecetane
Niger.summary: A large quantity of weapons and ammunition was seized by the Niger National Guard (GNN) in Ibecetane, in the rural municipality of Akoubounou, Abalak Department (Tahoua Region). This seizure was presented to the Governor of the region, Colonel-Major Souleymane Amadou Moussa, on Monday, 16 November 2026, on the premises of the Tahoua Regional District of the NGG.

Niger.title: Nigeria: The army is authorised to pursue armed fighters up to 5 km into Niger, Chad and Cameroon
Niger.summary: Abuja now wants to target armed groups beyond its borders. In an announcement made in Abuja on 16 November, Nigerian Defence Minister General Christopher Musa stated that his forces could cross the border by a maximum of five kilometres when pursuing attackers. Indeed, according to the Minister, Cameroon, Niger and Chad have agreed to this right of cross-border pursuit.

Niger.title: In Niger, Algeria is taking steps to secure its interests in the Sahel
Niger.summary: An Algerian army convoy arrived in Niger on 31 October, marking the first deployment of Algerian troops abroad. A first in 53 years! The last time Algeria sent troops abroad was in 1973, to support Egypt during the Arab-Israeli War.

Niger.title: In Niger, a terrorist logistics base...
Niger.summary: In Niger, a terrorist logistics base destroyed in the Tillabéry region The Niger National Guard neutralised two terrorists and dismantled a logistics base of armed terrorist groups located near Kobagué, in the Torodi Department, Tillabéry region. This was announced by the National Guard on 17 November in a press release. .

Niger.title: Niger: New attack in the Dosso region, in the south-west
Niger.summary: In Niger, an attack took place last week in the department of Dioundou, in the Dosso region, in the south-west of the country. For the time being, no official casualty figures have been released. A visit to the bereaved families following the terrorist attacks carried out in several villages in the rural commune of Dioundiou This is how the Nigerien news agency reported the visit on Saturday of Colonel Major Bana Alhassane, the Governor of the Dosso region, to the Dioundiou department, which borders Nigeria.

Niger.title: Nigeria: The country signs a new military agreement with Cameroon, Niger and Chad
Niger.summary: A new military agreement has been signed between Nigeria, Cameroon, Niger and Chad. It should enable Nigeria to pursue armed fighters beyond its borders. Nigeria now intends to be able to pursue armed fighters up to a five-kilometre strip in neighbouring territory.

Niger.title: New attack in the Dosso region, in south-western Niger
Niger.summary: In Niger, an attack took place last week in the Dioundou Department, in the Dosso region, in the south-west of the country. For the time being, no official casualty figures have been released. Published on: A visit to the bereaved families following the terrorist attacks carried out in several villages in the rural municipality of Dioundiou This is how the Nigerien news agency reported the visit on Saturday of Colonel Major Bana Alhassane, the Governor of the Dosso region, to the department of Dioundiou, which borders Nigeria.

Niger.title: Nigeria signs a new military agreement with Cameroon, Niger and Chad
Niger.summary: A new military agreement has been concluded between Nigeria, Cameroon, Niger and Chad. It should enable Nigeria to pursue armed fighters beyond its borders. Published on: Nigeria now intends to be able to pursue armed fighters up to a distance of five kilometres into neighbouring territory .

Mali.title: Previous Mali: 1,505 fuel tankers in Bamako
Mali.summary: In total, 1,505 tanker trucks carrying petroleum products have arrived in Bamako since the beginning of November, including 840 new vehicles recently received, according to a supply report shared by several media outlets on Monday, 16 November 2026. This new delivery follows the arrival of 665 tankers on 7 November, escorted by the Malian Armed Forces (FAMa), against a backdrop of persistent disruptions to hydrocarbon supply chains.

Mali.title: Mali: Assimi Goïta equips the Army with 7 new combat and transport aircraft
Mali.summary: The official handover of the keys to the seven aircraft took place at the presidential pavilion of Bamako-Senou's President Modibo Keïta International Airport, in the presence of senior military officials, members of the government, the diplomatic corps and several other dignitaries. This new acquisition represents a significant strengthening of the Malian Air Force's fleet.

Mali.title: Africa More than 68,000 Burkinabés repatriated from Guinea following measures against illegal gold mining
Mali.summary: Illegal gold miners deported to Burkina Faso by Guinea-Conakry, in Bamako, on 10 November 2026. More than 68,000 Burkinabé nationals have been repatriated from Guinea since the start of operations led by Conakry against illegal gold mining, the authorities in Ouagadougou announced in a statement seen by AFP on Tuesday. .

Mali.source: AMAP (Agence Malienne de Presse et de Publicité)
Mali.title: GMS–Samé–Kati roundabout section: demolition operations launched to clear the project rights-of-way
Mali.summary: Bamako, 17 November (AMAP) The demolition of buildings and structures located within the right-of-way of the GMS Roundabout–Samé–Kati section began on Monday, 16 November 2020, AMAP learned from an official source. The announcement was made in a joint statement by the Ministers for Transport and Infrastructure, Urban Planning, Housing, State Property, Regional Planning and Population, which was published on Sunday evening.

Mali.title: More than 68,000 Burkinabe repatriated from Guinea following measures against illegal gold mining
Mali.summary: Since the beginning of November, Guinea has intensified operations against illegal gold panning, particularly in the gold-rich Siguiri region (northeast). The government accuses this activity of causing significant environmental damage and says it wants to put an end to the unregulated exploitation of mineral resources. .

Mali.source: AMAP (Agence Malienne de Presse et de Publicité)
Mali.title: Nioro du Sahel: The efforts of the FAMa are helping to revive economic activity and transport
Mali.summary: Nioro du Sahel, 17 November 2026 (AMAP) – The efforts of the Malian Armed Forces (FAMa) to improve security and facilitate the free movement of people and goods are contributing to the gradual return to normality in Nioro du Sahel. . The arrival of several dozen fuel tankers, the resumption of transport links with Bamako and Kayes, and the restocking of markets are all signs of this improvement after nine months of severe disruption.

Mali.title: Air Force: The fleet is gaining in heavy transport and mobility
Mali.summary: CURRENTLY From January to October 2026, the Malian Air Force carried out more than 7,000 sorties, totalling nearly 26,000 flight hours. Brigadier General Alou Boï Diarra, Chief of Staff of this component, also reported that around 28,000 passengers and more than 2,000 tonnes of cargo were transported during this period. .

Mali.title: Mali: The FAMa target bases and...
Mali.summary: Mali: The FAMa target bases and logistics depots of armed groups in Abeïbara and Sévaré The Malian Armed Forces (FAMa) have carried out new precision strikes against positions of armed terrorist groups in the Abeïbara and Sévaré sectors . These operations, carried out on 14 and 16 November 2026 as part of Operation Dougoukoloko, targeted assembly points housing armed individuals and military equipment, according to the General Staff of the Armed Forces.

Mali.title: Mali: Nearly 80,000 people expelled from Guinea already repatriated, 13 deaths recorded
Mali.summary: The Centre for Crisis Coordination and Management (CECOGEC), a Malian government body, announced on 16 November 2026 that 79,044 people deported from Guinea have already returned home, thanks to 522 vehicles, including 421 lorries and 101 coaches. Thirteen deaths were also recorded during the operations. .

Mali.title: Malian Armed Forces: New aircraft to dominate the skies
Mali.summary: Our country has just taken a historic step, thereby confirming its inexorable progress towards strategic defence autonomy across the entire national territory. Yesterday, the Transitional President and Supreme Commander of the Armed Forces, Army General Assimi Goïta, handed over a substantial consignment of air equipment to the Malian Armed Forces (FAMa). .

Mali.title: Air Force: Over 7,000 sorties and 26,000 flight hours completed in ten months
Mali.summary: The Malian Air Force carried out more than 7,000 sorties, totalling nearly 26,000 flight hours between January and October 2026. During this period, it also transported around 28,000 passengers and more than 2,000 tonnes of cargo. These figures were announced on Monday, 16 November 2026, by the Chief of Staff of the Air Force, Brigadier General Alou Boï Diarra, on the occasion of the official handover of new aircraft to the Malian Armed Forces (FAMa).

Mali.title: ORGANISED CRIME IN SIKASSO: A FAKE SOLDIER ARRESTED
Mali.summary: An individual who was impersonating a sergeant in the Malian Armed Forces (FAMa) was arrested in Sikasso in recent days for falsely claiming a title. This arrest is reminiscent of a previous case recorded in the same town in October 2024, when a bogus customs officer was arrested for (…) By Mahamane TOURE – NOUVEL HORIZON

Mali.title: Mali: The FAMa carry out precision strikes against terrorist groups in Abeibara and Sévaré
Mali.summary: The General Staff of the Armed Forces informs the national public that the Malian Armed Forces (FAMa), supported by their partners, are continuing their ongoing operations to monitor, control and secure the national territory as part of Operation Dougoukoloko. . On Saturday, 14 November 2026, a gathering point for armed terrorist groups, housing several individuals as well as military equipment, including vehicles and a fuel depot, was the target of precision strikes between eight (8) and ten (10) kilometres north and north-east of Abeïbara.

Mali.title: Mali: 13 people deported from Guinea found dead
Mali.summary: The deportations of Malian and Burkinabé nationals from gold mining areas in Guinea have resulted in 13 deaths in Mali, while 79,044 people have been transported as part of return operations, according to a report from the Centre for Coordination and Crisis Management (CECOGEC), published on Monday, 16 November 2026. These figures illustrate the scale of this humanitarian crisis, which has been mobilising the Malian and Burkinabé authorities, health services and aid organisations for several weeks.

Mali.title: Mali: 1,505 fuel tankers in Bamako
Mali.summary: In total, 1,505 tanker trucks carrying petroleum products have arrived in Bamako since the beginning of November, including 840 new vehicles recently received, according to a supply report shared by several media outlets on Monday, 16 November 2020. . This new arrival follows the receipt of 665 tankers on 7 November, under escort by the Malian Armed Forces (FAMa), in a context marked by persistent disruptions to hydrocarbon supply chains.

Mali.title: Mali-Russia: Seven new aircraft strengthen the military fleet
Mali.summary: On Monday, 16 November 2026, the Malian army took delivery of seven new aircraft acquired as part of its military cooperation with Russia, comprising one strategic transport aircraft and six helicopters, intended to strengthen its mobility, logistical transport and air support capabilities. . The handover ceremony, presided over by the Head of State, Army General Assimi Goïta, took place at Bamako-Sénou's President Modibo Keïta International Airport, in the presence of several government and military officials.

Mali.title: Mali: Assimi Goïta hands over an Ilyushin IL-76 aircraft and Mi-24 and Mi-8 helicopters to the Air Force
Mali.summary: On Monday, 16 November 2026, the President of Mali's Transitional Government, Army General Assimi Goïta, officially handed over new aircraft to the Malian Armed Forces (FAMa) at Modibo Keïta-Sénou International Airport. . Comprising an IL-76 strategic transport aircraft and Mi-24 and Mi-8 helicopters, this equipment is intended to strengthen the operational, logistical and air capabilities of the Malian army.

Mali.title: Mali: New military aircraft to strengthen the Army's capabilities
Mali.summary: On Monday, 16 November 2020, at Président Modibo KEÏTA-Sénou International Airport, the Transitional President, Head of State and Supreme Commander of the Armed Forces, Army General Assimi GOÏTA, officially handed over the keys to an Ilyushin IL-76 strategic transport aircraft and Mi-24 and Mi-8 helicopters to the Malian Armed Forces (FAMa). . This acquisition, funded by the State, strengthens the operational and logistical capabilities of the national defence force and reflects the commitment of the highest authorities to continue efforts to modernise the defence force.

Mali.title: Guinea: A government delegation from Mali visits Conakry
Mali.summary: CONAKRY – A high-level ministerial delegation from the Republic of Mali arrived in Conakry on Tuesday, 10 November 2026. Led by the Minister of Mines, Professor Amadou Keïta, the delegation was welcomed on arrival by the Chief of Staff of Guinea's Ministry of Mines and Geology. This official visit is part of the Malian authorities' participation in the first edition of the Simandou Mining Summit, which is scheduled to open this Wednesday, 11 November, on Kassa Island, Africaguinee.com has learned from sources close to the department headed by Bouna Sylla.

Burkina Faso.title: IP-P3A: The Coris Foundation donates 360 motorised tricycles to agricultural VDPs
Burkina Faso.summary: On Tuesday, 17 November 2026, the Coris Foundation officially handed over 360 tricycle motorcycles to the Agricultural Volunteers for the Defence of the Homeland (VDP). The formal ceremony took place at the headquarters of the National Office for Major Projects in Burkina Faso (BN-GPB). This donation will help to strengthen local production and rural logistics throughout the country.

Burkina Faso.title: Coup Leaders’ Promises Fall Short
Burkina Faso.summary: Military leaders in Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger overthrew democratically elected governments, arguing that those governments had failed to suppress long-running insurgencies that junta leaders claimed they could put down. Years later, however, experts say that those juntas, like others before them, are failing their citizens in multiple ways. “A coup is not necessarily the most effective way to cure economic and political ills,” economist John Mukum Mbaku recently wrote for The Conversation.

Niger.title: Niger: A terrorist logistics base dismantled near Torodi
Niger.summary: The Nigerien army has announced that it has dismantled a logistics base belonging to armed terrorist groups near Kobagué, in the department of Torodi (Tillabéry region), in western Niger. The operation was carried out during the night of Monday 16 to Tuesday 17 November. This was a night raid led by the Torodi National Guard Squadron and the Alpha Zero Unit.

Niger.title: NDLEA arrests eight over cocaine shipment to Europe
Niger.summary: Operatives of the National Drug Law Enforcement Agency have arrested eight members of a transnational drug trafficking cartel accused of moving cocaine from Lagos through Kano, Niger Republic and Libya to Europe. The suspects, who allegedly swallowed cocaine pellets to evade security checks, excreted a total of 634 wraps weighing 13.795 kilogrammes while in NDLEA custody.

Niger.title: Niger: President Tiani makes new appointments to the senior administration
Niger.summary: On Monday, 16 November 2020, the President of the Republic, Head of State, General Abdourahmane Tiani, signed several decrees concerning individual measures. . According to the press release issued by the Minister, Secretary General of the Government, this concerns a series of appointments to senior positions in several key ministries (Defence, Interior, Foreign Affairs, Health, Infrastructure, Transport, etc.), as well as in the central administration and at the head of public institutions.

Niger.title: Celebration of the 15th edition of African Road Safety Day: ANISER conducts a major roadside inspection operation in Niamey
Niger.summary: As part of the celebrations for the 15th edition of African Road Safety Day, the Nigerien Road Safety Agency (ANISER) organised a major road safety check operation in the city of Niamey on Sunday, 15 November 2020. . Conducted jointly with the National Police, the National Gendarmerie and the Municipal Police, this operation aims to ensure that road users, namely motorcyclists and motorists, comply with the Highway Code.

Niger.title: NDLEA arrests eight cocaine couriers, recovers 634 wraps
Niger.summary: Operatives of the National Drug Law Enforcement Agency have arrested eight members of a transnational drug trafficking cartel accused of moving cocaine from Lagos through Kano, Niger Republic and Libya to Europe. The suspects, who allegedly swallowed cocaine pellets to evade security checks, excreted a total of 634 wraps weighing 13.795 kilogrammes while in NDLEA custody.

Niger.title: Niger: Appointment of New Secretaries General to the Ministries of Defence and the Interior
Niger.summary: Niamey, 17 November (ANP) – Brigadier General MAMANE SOULEY, General Officer of the Nigerien Armed Forces, has been appointed Secretary General of the Ministry of National Defence, while Colonel Major NOMA DARI has been promoted to Deputy Secretary General, according to a decree issued by the President of the Republic and made public on 16 November 2026. . At the Ministry of the Interior, Public Security and Territorial Administration, Police Commissioner General Ayouba Abdou Rahamane has been appointed Secretary General of the said ministry, according to the same source.

Niger.title: Customs cooperation: Nigerian trainee officers on an immersion programme in Niamey to familiarise themselves with border security strategies
Niger.summary: As part of the cooperation between the customs administrations of Niger and Nigeria, thirteen (13) trainee officers from the Nigerian Customs Service (NCS) will be carrying out a study visit in Niamey from 14 to 21 November 2026, in order to analyse the experience of their counterparts from the Nigerien Directorate General of Customs (DGD) in combating transnational threats.

Niger.title: Niger: Police Commissioner General Aboubacar Issaka Oumarou, new Director General of the National Police
Niger.summary: Niamey, 17 November (ANP) – Police Commissioner General Aboubacar Issaka Oumarou, formerly Director of the Central Office for the Suppression of Illicit Drug Trafficking (OCRTIS), has been appointed Director General of the National Police (DGPN), by decree signed on 13 November by the President of the Republic, Army General Abdourahamane Tiani. . With several years of experience in the field of public safety, the new Director General of the National Police has a professional career marked by significant responsibilities in Niger and abroad.

Niger.title: Tahoua: Significant quantity of weapons and ammunition seized in Ibecetane
Niger.summary: Tahoua, 17 November (ANP) – A large quantity of weapons and ammunition has been seized by the Niger National Guard (GNN) in Ibecetane, in the Rural Commune of Akoubounou, Abalak Department (Tahoua Region). This seizure was presented to the Governor of the Region, Colonel-Major Souleymane Amadou Moussa, on Monday, 16 November 2026, on the premises of the Tahoua Regional District of the GNN.

Niger.title: Niger: A new Director General at the head of the DGPN
Niger.summary: Niamey, 16 November (ANP) – On Friday, 13 November 2020, the President of the Republic, Army General Abdourahamane Tiani, signed two decrees appointing the new Director General and Deputy Director General of the National Police (DGPN). This concerns Chief Police Commissioner Aboubacar Issaka Oumarou, Service No. 50 865, appointed Head of the General Directorate of the National Police (DGPN), and Divisional Police Commissioner Abdoulaye Maman Mijinyawa, Service No.

Mali.title: Strengthening the operational capabilities of the FAMa: The Transitional President presents new aircraft to the Air Force
Mali.summary: On Monday, 16 November 2020, at Modibo Keïta-Sénou International Airport, the Transitional President, Head of State and Supreme Commander of the Armed Forces, Army General Assimi Goïta, officially handed over the keys to an Ilyushin IL-76 strategic transport aircraft and Mi-24 and Mi-8 helicopters to the Malian Armed Forces (FAMa). . This acquisition strengthens the operational and logistical capabilities of the national defence force.

Mali.title: Operation Dougoukoloko: The army strikes terrorist positions in Abeïbara and Sévaré
Mali.summary: According to the press release, the first assembly point, located between 8 and 10 kilometres north and north-east of Abeïbara, housed several individuals as well as military equipment, including vehicles, and a fuel depot. The second, located 33 kilometres south-west of Sévaré, also housed several individuals and military equipment, including motorcycles. .

Mali.title: Mali: The army receives a new batch of aircraft
Mali.summary: Mali: The army takes delivery of a new batch of aircraft The Malian army is expanding its air fleet. On Monday, 16 November 2026, it took delivery of a new batch of aircraft on the tarmac of the presidential pavilion at Modibo Keita International Airport in Bamako. The Transitional President, Army General Assimi Goïta, presided over the ceremony in the presence of civil and military authorities.

Mali.title: Bamako: The body of a man pulled from the Niger River
Mali.summary: A body was removed from the Niger River on Sunday evening, in Badalabougou, near the Martyrs' Bridge. It was fishermen who spotted it and raised the alarm. The victim is a man of about 30 years old.

Mali.title: STRENGTHENING OPERATIONAL CAPABILITIES: The Transitional President presents a new batch of aircraft to the Malian Armed Forces
Mali.summary: On Monday, 16 November 2026, the Supreme Commander of the Armed Forces, Army General Assimi Goïta, presided over the official ceremony at the Presidential Pavilion of Modibo Keïta-Sénou International Airport for the handover of new aircraft to the Malian Armed Forces. This allocation reflects the desire of the highest authorities to continue efforts to modernise the defence force.

Mali.title: National Defence: The Air Force is strengthening its fleet with an IL-76 strategic aircraft and Mi-24 and Mi-8 helicopters
Mali.summary: STRENGTHENING THE OPERATIONAL CAPABILITIES OF THE FAMa: The Transitional President hands over new aircraft to the Air Force The Transitional President, Head of State and Supreme Commander of the Armed Forces, Army General Assimi Goïta, officially handed over the keys to an Ilyushin IL-76 strategic transport aircraft and Mi-24 and Mi-17 helicopters at Président Modibo Keïta-Sénou International Airport on Monday, 16 November 2026.

Mali.source: AMAP (Agence Malienne de Presse et de Publicité)
Mali.title: Mali: The National Defence Forces Equipped with New Aircraft
Mali.summary: Bamako, 16 November (AMAP) The official ceremony for the handover of new aircraft was presided over on Monday at Modibo Keïta – Sénou International Airport by the Transitional President, Army General Assimi Goïta, in the presence of civil and military authorities, AMAP reported. . This new batch of aircraft includes an Ilyushin Il-76 strategic transport aircraft, four Mi-8 utility helicopters and two Mi-24 attack helicopters.

Mali.title: Mali: Assimi Goïta equips the army with 7 new military aircraft, including 4 Mi-24 helicopters
Mali.summary: On Monday, 16 November 2026, the President of Mali's Transitional Government, Army General Assimi Goïta, presided over a ceremony at Bamako's Président Modibo Keïta International Airport to hand over new aircraft to the Malian Armed Forces (FAMa). This delivery covers seven aircraft. These include four Mi-24 attack helicopters, two Mi-8 utility helicopters and one Ilyushin Il-76 strategic transport aircraft.

Mali.title: Defence: Mali strengthens its air fleet with seven new aircraft
Mali.summary: On Monday, 16 November 2026, the Malian Armed Forces (FAMa) took delivery of seven new aircraft to enhance their operational capabilities. Funded entirely from the national budget as part of cooperation with Russia, this equipment includes a strategic transport aircraft, four utility helicopters and two attack helicopters. .

Mali.title: GMS roundabout–Samé–Kati section: The...
Mali.summary: GMS roundabout–Samé–Kati section: The demolition of buildings and installations within the project's right-of-way begins this Monday, 16 November 2026. The demolition of buildings and installations located within the right-of-way of the GMS Roundabout–Samé–Kati section will begin this Monday The announcement was made by the Ministers of Transport and Infrastructure, Urban Planning, Housing, State Property, Regional Planning and Population in a joint statement released on Sunday evening.

Mali.title: The Malian Air Force receives new helicopters and a transport aircraft
Mali.summary: The Malian Armed Forces (FAMa) are strengthening their air fleet. On Monday, 16 November, the Transitional President and Supreme Commander of the Armed Forces, Army General Assimi Goïta, presided over the handover ceremony for new aircraft at Modibo Keïta International Airport in Bamako, in the presence of the military hierarchy. .

Mali.title: GMS roundabout–Samé–Kati section: The demolition of buildings and installations within the project's right-of-way will begin on Monday, 16 November 2026.
Mali.summary: The announcement was made by the Ministers of Transport and Infrastructure, Urban Planning, Housing, State Property, Regional Planning and Population in a joint statement released on Sunday evening. According to the press release, this operation is part of the clearing of the rights of way essential for carrying out the dual carriageway development works on this important section of road.

Mali.title: Guinea deports 1,557 West African nationals after they were convicted of illegal gold mining
Mali.summary: The Guinean authorities deported 1,557 citizens from West African countries, mostly from Mali and Burkina Faso, to their countries of origin, after they were convicted of illegal gold mining, according to Radio France Internationale. The radio station reported that the deportation operation took place on Saturday, 14 November, involving 44 vehicles and helicopters, and under tight security.

Mali.title: Guinea-Mali border: 1,557 gold miners of various nationalities tried, pardoned and deported to Kourémalé
Mali.summary: Guinea-Mali border: 1,557 gold panners of various nationalities tried, pardoned and deported to Kourémalé On Friday, 13 November 2026, the Guinean authorities released 1,557 people of various nationalities who had been arrested at mining sites for illegal gold panning activities. . According to our information, all these individuals were tried by various Guinean courts before being pardoned by the Head of State and deported to the Malian border.

Mali.title: Guinea: Is JNIM threatening the country from Mali? What a field study reveals
Mali.summary: On 25 October 2026, the Konrad Adenauer Foundation published a study on the establishment of JNIM, a group linked to al-Qaeda, in south-western Mali, on the border with Guinea. Conducted by the SITOC organisation in June and July 2026, the survey is based on 68 testimonies collected in south-western Mali and Upper Guinea. Local officials, representatives of civil society, security stakeholders, gold miners and transhumant herders were interviewed.

Mali.title: Kourémalé: 1,557 gold miners of various nationalities pardoned and escorted to the Guinea-Mali border
Mali.summary: A total of 1,557 gold miners of various nationalities, who were arrested at mining sites for "illegal gold mining activities", were tried and sentenced in Conakry. They were granted a pardon on Friday, 13 November 2020, and then taken to Kourémalé, on the border between Guinea and Mali, on Saturday, 14 November, by the Guinean authorities, with a view to returning them to their respective countries.

Mali.title: Mali: Mauritania, the Maghreb country most exposed to the crisis, according to the IEEE
Mali.summary: On 13 November 2023, the Spanish Institute for Strategic Studies (IEEE) published an analysis identifying Mauritania as the Maghreb country most directly threatened by the deteriorating situation in Mali. Authored by analyst Jaime Bello, the text specifies that his views do not represent the position of the Spanish Ministry of Defence. According to him, Nouakchott is under three pressures at once: a porous border, the terrorist threat and the mass influx of refugees.

Mali.title: Kayes: A 45-year-old suspect arrested for sexually abusing an 8-year-old girl
Mali.summary: As part of Operation 'KOKADJÈ', initiated by the Regional Director of the National Police of Kayes, Chief Superintendent Tapa Oury Diallo, the Police Station of the 1st Arrondissement of Kayes, headed by Chief Superintendent Daouda Cissé, arrested an individual suspected of sexually abusing an eight-year-old girl on 7 November 2024. . Alerted by a complaint from the victim's family, the police immediately began investigations that led to the arrest of the suspect, identified by the initials M.T., aged 45 and residing in the Lafiabougou-Faradabougouni district in Kayes.

Mali.title: Illegal gold mining: Is what is prohibited in Guinea permitted in Mali?
Mali.summary: Illegal gold panning: Is what is prohibited in Guinea permitted in Mali? Since the beginning of this month, Mali has been facing an influx into its territory of several nationals from the subregion, particularly from Burkina Faso. They are being turned away from Guinea-Conakry due to illegal gold panning.

Mali.title: Kadianna and Boulkessi: The FAMa strike several positions of armed terrorist groups
Mali.summary: Kadianna and Boulkessi: FAMa strike several positions of armed terrorist groups Maliweb

Mali.title: Military cooperation: Bamako and AFRICOM explore possibilities for US support
Mali.summary: Journal du Mali

Mali.title: FAMa: Three airstrikes against terrorist positions in Kidal, Timbuktu and Sikasso
Mali.summary: Maliweb

Burkina Faso.title: Burkina Faso: 100 new stars to illuminate Avenue Kwame-Nkrumah
Burkina Faso.summary: One hundred Burkinabé and foreign personalities now have their stars on Avenue Kwame-Nkrumah, in the heart of Ouagadougou. Their names are engraved on stelae installed as part of the second edition of the "Street of Stars", an initiative of the Sotigui Academy. .

Burkina Faso.title: Defence: The FAMa are strengthening their fleet with new aircraft acquired using their own funds
Burkina Faso.summary: The official handover ceremony was presided over by the Supreme Commander of the Armed Forces, Army General Assimi Goïta, in the presence of civil and military authorities. Fully funded from the national budget and acquired as part of cooperation with the Russian Federation, these aircraft are intended to increase the army's strategic mobility and logistical autonomy.

Burkina Faso.title: AES: Ministers prepare for the upcoming summit in Ouagadougou
Burkina Faso.summary: The three countries reviewed the implementation of the Year II roadmap. Operational decisions are expected at the next College of Heads of State. The Extraordinary Council of Ministers of the Confederation of Sahel States met on 11 and 12 November in Ouagadougou.

Burkina Faso.title: The legal front
Burkina Faso.summary: On Friday, 13 November 2020, the Public Prosecutor at the Ouagadougou Court of Appeal held a press briefing on the legal proceedings brought against 45 individuals and legal entities for various offences related to terrorism and breaches of public order. . This statement by the judicial authorities serves as a reminder that, in a state facing a war that threatens its very existence, the defence of the nation is not limited to fighting terrorists.

Burkina Faso.title: Legal proceedings: landmark cases revealed
Burkina Faso.summary: On Friday, 13 November 2020, Pinguedewindé Désiré Sawadogo, the Public Prosecutor at the Ouagadougou Court of Appeal, held a press conference in Ouagadougou on the status of certain cases currently under investigation at the Specialised Judicial Division for the Suppression of Acts of Terrorism of the Ouaga II High Court. . Since 30 September 2022, under the leadership of the President of Burkina Faso, Captain Ibrahim Traoré, Burkina Faso has been waging a successful and fearless fight against terrorism.

Niger.title: African Road Safety Day: Niger focuses on discipline and strengthening checks to reduce road accidents
Niger.summary: Le Niger a célébré, le dimanche 15 novembre 2026, la 15è édition de la Journée africaine de la sécurité routière sous le thème : « Zéro tolérance sur nos routes : sensibiliser, contrôler, inspecter et réprimer ». Instituée par l’Union africaine, cette journée est observée chaque troisième dimanche du mois de novembre. Elle est couplée à la Journée mondiale du souvenir des victimes des accidents de la route, une journée officielle des Nations Unies.

Niger.title: NATIONAL POLICE: GENERAL ABOUBACAR OUMAROU, A SEASONED OFFICER AT THE HELM
Niger.summary: From the fight against illicit drug trafficking to command responsibilities within the National Police, Police Commissioner General Aboubacar Issaka Oumarou is taking the helm of the DGPN. His career has been marked by professional experience in Niger and in several international United Nations missions. The General Directorate of the National Police (DGPN) has a new head .

Niger.title: 15th edition of the JASR: 7,116 accidents resulted in 1,245 deaths and 4,439 serious injuries in Niger in 2023
Niger.summary: Niamey, 15 November (ANP) – In a message delivered on Saturday, 14 November, the day before the celebration of the 15th edition of African Road Safety Day, the Minister of Transport and Civil Aviation, Colonel Major Abdourahamane Amadou, announced that, in 2025, Niger had recorded 7,116 road accidents, which resulted in 1,245 deaths and 4,439 serious injuries in the country.

Mali.title: PRAYERS AND REFLECTION: The Catholic Church of Mali pays tribute to the military personnel and civilians who have fallen in the service of the Nation
Mali.summary: On Sunday, 15 November 2026, the Catholic Church of Mali held a Eucharistic celebration in memory of the soldiers and civilians who fell while carrying out their duty in the service of the nation. The ceremony took place at Bamako's Cathedral of the Sacred Heart, presided over by Archbishop Robert Cissé, Metropolitan Archbishop of Bamako, in the presence of the Chief of the General Staff of the Armed Forces, Major General Elisée Jean Dao, and a large military delegation.

Mali.title: Yenchechi, Kidal and Ingouzma: The FAMa...
Mali.summary: Yenchechi, Kidal and Ingouzma: The FAMa neutralise terrorist targets In a statement issued on Saturday, 14 November 2026, the General Staff of the Armed Forces provided an update on the recent operations carried out by the Malian Armed Forces (FAMa), supported by their partners, as part of Operation Dougoukoloko. . Several terrorist bases and hideouts were successfully destroyed during patrols and precision strikes.

Mali.title: Sikasso: A fake sergeant arrested by the security forces
Mali.summary: Sikasso: A fake sergeant arrested by law enforcement A civilian who presented himself as an army sergeant was arrested in Sikasso by law enforcement. The man was arrested after arousing suspicion. He is currently being questioned to determine the reasons for this identity theft.

Mali.title: Guinea-Mali border: 1,557 gold miners of various nationalities released and taken to Kourémalé
Mali.summary: On Friday, 13 November 2026, the Guinean authorities released 1,557 people of various nationalities who had been arrested at mining sites for illegal gold mining activities, according to a report published on the Facebook page of the Guinean Ministry of Defence. . These individuals, after being tried in Conakry, received a presidential pardon and were then taken on Saturday, 14 November to Kourémalé, a town located on the border between Guinea and Mali.

Burkina Faso.title: Road traffic: “No urgency, no social pressure… can justify putting your life or the lives of others at risk”
Burkina Faso.summary: This is a message from the Burkinabe Minister of Security on the occasion of the commemoration of the World Day of Remembrance for Road Traffic Victims, together with the 18th edition of the National Road Safety Awareness Day.

Burkina Faso.title: Road safety in Burkina Faso: Minister Mahamadou Sana declares an end to tolerance of antisocial behaviour on the roads
Burkina Faso.summary: On the occasion of the 18th National Road Safety Awareness Day, celebrated on 15 November 2024, coinciding with the World Day of Remembrance for Road Traffic Victims, the Minister of Security, Mahamadou Sana, issues a firm call for individual responsibility and collective. His message was made public on Sunday, 15 November, by the Ministry of Security. With the theme “Zero tolerance for anti-social behaviour on the roads”, the government intends to strengthen prevention, checks and enforcement of the law to better protect human lives.

Burkina Faso.title: Road safety in Burkina Faso: Minister Mahamadou Sana calls for 'zero tolerance for antisocial behaviour on the roads'
Burkina Faso.summary: On the occasion of the 18th National Road Safety Awareness Day, together with the World Day of Remembrance for Road Traffic Victims, the Minister of Security, Mahamadou Sana, is calling on road users to be more responsible and to strictly comply with the Highway Code. This year's event is themed "Zero tolerance for antisocial behaviour on the roads" . On 15 November 2026, Burkina Faso will commemorate the 18th National Road Safety Awareness Day (JNSSR).

Niger.title: Niger: 5 mercenaries neutralised and several items of military equipment seized from 1 to 12 November
Niger.summary: Niamey, 15 Nov (ANP) – The Integrated Operations Coordination Centre reports that, according to the assessment for 1 to 12 November 2025, the Defence and Security Forces neutralised 5 mercenaries and seized several items of military equipment. This includes three mercenary lookouts stationed on a hill, who were neutralised in the Samira sector during a presence patrol carried out by Operation Niya on 3 November.

Niger.title: Thousands of Arab Nomads Ordered to Leave Niger
Niger.summary: Several thousand Arab nomads from the Mahamid tribe, who have lived for decades in southeastern Niger, have been told to leave the country by the end of the year, local authorities said Sunday. Niger’s military regime has accused the Mahamid of supplying weapons and logistics to Boko Haram terrorists active in the region. “This is a very firm directive from the country’s highest authorities: the Mahamid must return home by December 31, 2026 — a strict deadline,” a senior official in Niger’s Diffa region told AFP.

Niger.title: Niger: At least 30 civilians killed by "armed men" in the west, according to local sources cited by AFP
Niger.summary: Niger: At least 30 civilians killed by 'armed men' in the west, according to local sources cited by AFP Published on: Advertisement At least 30 civilians were killed on 12 November 2026 in an ambush by unidentified 'armed men' near Téra, in western Niger, close to Burkina Faso and Mali, AFP learned on Friday from local sources. . The attack targeted residents of the village of Tillim, "very close to Téra, killing 37 people, including women and children", said a resident of the town of Téra.

Burkina Faso.title: The Burkinabé diaspora in Côte d'Ivoire donates 3,000 school bags to the orphans of the DSF and VDP who fell at the front
Burkina Faso.summary: (Ouagadougou, 13 November 2026) Professor Zakaria SORÉ, National Coordinator of the Presidential Initiative for Quality Education for All (IPEQ) and Minister and Secretary General of the Presidency of Burkina Faso, has received a donation of 3,000 schoolbags for the orphans of members of the combat forces who have fallen at the front.

Burkina Faso.title: Burkina Faso orders arrest of journalists, activists over terrorism allegations
Burkina Faso.summary: Burkinabe authorities said on Friday they had issued arrest warrants for some 20 people, including journalists, activists, a former minister and former officers in exile over alleged “terrorism” offences. Ouagadougou Court of Appeal attorney general Desire Sawadogo said 14 arrest warrants with extradition requests had been issued, alongside seven further standard warrants.

Burkina Faso.title: Burkina Faso: International arrest warrant issued against Camille Makosso for alleged terrorism
Burkina Faso.summary: . The Burkinabé judiciary has taken a new step in its judicial offensive against alleged supporters of terrorism. .

Burkina Faso.title: The Burkinabe diaspora in Côte d'Ivoire donates 3,000 school bags to the orphans of the DSF and VDP who fell at the front
Burkina Faso.summary: PRESIDENTIAL INITIATIVE FOR QUALITY EDUCATION FOR ALL The Burkinabé diaspora in Côte d'Ivoire donates 3,000 schoolbags to the orphans of the Defence and Security Forces (FDS) and Volunteer Defence Fighters (VDP) who fell at the front (Ouagadougou, 13 November 2024) Professor Zakaria SORÉ, National Coordinator of the Presidential Initiative for Quality Education for All (IPEQ) and also Minister and Secretary General of the Presidency of Burkina Faso, received a donation of 3,000 schoolbags.

Burkina Faso.title: Burkina Faso’s rival armed groups turn on each other as state loses ground
Burkina Faso.summary: Ouagadougou, Burkina Faso – Armed fighters from two rival groups have fought a series of increasingly deadly battles along Burkina Faso’s northern border with Mali, as the government struggles to reassert control over large parts of the country. The clashes between Jama’at Nusrat al-Islam wal Muslimin (JNIM), an al-Qaeda affiliate, and the ISIL affiliate in Sahel Province (ISSP) have intensified since early September, with both groups competing for territory and influence across the borderlands.

Burkina Faso.title: Burkina Faso: 100 distinguished figures honoured at the second edition of the Rue des Étoiles
Burkina Faso.summary: On Friday, 13 November 2026, the Sotigui Awards Academy unveiled new plaques on Avenue Kwamé N'Krumah in Ouagadougou. This second edition honoured and immortalised 100 figures from Burkina Faso and abroad for their careers, their commitment and their contributions in their respective fields. .

Niger.title: Editorial: Tell me your tall tales, and I'll tell you who you are
Niger.summary: If we are to speak in broad terms about the European Union, and to speak exclusively about its relations with Niger since 26 July 2023, we should point out, without embellishment, its high-level paternalism, mention the neo-colonialism that characterises it to the highest degree, highlight its perfidy, which has reached its highest level, and emphasise its duplicity, characterised by a high level of vacillation.

Niger.title: "Information must originate from the regions, provinces and municipalities" (Minister Pingdwendé Gilbert Ouédraogo)
Niger.summary: Niamey, 13 November (AIB-ANP) – “Information must originate from the regions, provinces and municipalities. Today, by establishing ourselves in Bobo-Dioulasso, we aim to promote these initiatives. "Our country needs high-quality information more than anything else," said Burkina Faso's Minister for Communication, Pingdwendé Gilbert Ouédraogo, on Friday, 13 November 2020, at the official opening of the AIB's Guiriko regional office.

Niger.title: Niger: Over 30 civilians killed in an attack near Téra, in the Tillabéri region
Niger.summary: In Niger, an attack took place on Thursday 12 November in the Tillabéri region, in the west of the country, the epicentre of terrorist violence. It took place near the town of Téra, close to Burkina Faso and Mali. No official statements or casualty figures at this stage .

Niger.title: Gunmen kill at least 37 civilians in western Niger
Niger.summary: At least 37 civilians were killed on Thursday in an ambush by unidentified gunmen near Tera in western Niger, along the border with Burkina Faso and Mali, local sources told AFP. A former elected official said that the attack targeted residents of the village of Tilim as they were heading to the weekly market in Tera, a town and department of the same name in the Tillabéri Region (west).

Niger.title: Niger: At least 37 civilians killed by "armed men" in the west
Niger.summary: Members of the anti-jihadist special forces are patrolling the Tillabéri region, which is plagued by deadly attacks, on 6 November 2021 in Niger. At least 37 civilians were killed on Thursday in an ambush set by unidentified "armed men" near Téra, in western Niger, a region close to Burkina Faso and Mali that has become the epicentre of jihadist attacks, AFP learned from local sources on Friday.

Niger.title: Gunmen kill at least 37 civilians in western Niger
Niger.summary: At least 37 civilians were killed on Thursday in an ambush by unidentified gunmen near Tera in western Niger, along the border with Burkina Faso and Mali, according to local sources cited by Agence France-Presse. A former elected official said that the attack targeted the residents of the village of Tilim as they were heading to the weekly market in Tera, a city and department of the same name in the Tillabéri Region (west).

Niger.title: Niger: 38 civilians killed in an ambush near Téra
Niger.summary: The deadly attack near Téra, which claimed the lives of 38 people, including women and children, highlights the escalation of jihadist violence in an already troubled region of Niger, close to the borders with Mali and Burkina Faso. . At least 37 civilians were killed on Thursday in an ambush by unidentified "armed men" near Téra, in western Niger, close to Burkina Faso and Mali, AFP learned from local sources on Friday.

Niger.title: Niger: At least 37 civilians killed in an ambush by "armed men"

Niger.title: Niger: "In response to the arrival of...
Niger.summary: For Ibrahim Namaiwa, the presence of Algerian soldiers in Niger stems directly from the cooperation agreements between the two countries. He believes that securing major joint projects, particularly the Trans-Saharan Highway and oil exploitation, justifies this military cooperation. .
